To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of a lower selection pressure and postponing selection by 14 days after co-culturing are crucial for the recovery of transgenic oilseed rape plants.

the use of cotyledonary petiol and hypocotyl explants from seedlings grown under darkness conditions, a lower selection pressure and a 14-day delay of selection after co-culturation are essential factors in the transformation of oilseed rape.
the transformation of oilseed rape is possible with the use of a lower selection pressure, and that postponing of selection after co-culturing is an important step in the transformation process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a reliable protocol for genetic modification of economically important cultivars of oilseed rape, which can be used for the production of transgenic plants for further breeding.
the development of efficient transformation protocols of the economically important oilseed rapeseed cultivars Campino and Haydn.

establishing a protocol for Agrobacterium-mediated transformation and regeneration of the most widely used oilseed rape cultivar, Campino, and the first reports on transformation and regeneration of four other cultivars, Haydn, Hunter, Heros and Topas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transformation of oilseed rape is not a simple task.
the use of hypocotyls as a source of tissue for transformation is more efficient than use of cotyledonary petiolis.
the most effective protocol for transformation and regeneration of oilseed rape was established and that the obtained results are comparable to those obtained for other cultivars.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transformation of oilseed rape is a feasible technique, which is dependent upon the cultivar used and the type of explant used.

the transformation of B. napus cultivars is possible with a wide range of explant material and with different Agrobacterium strains, and the transformation efficiency can be increased by lowering of the antibiotic concentration in selection medium and postponing of the selection.

the use of hypocotyls and cotyledonary petiolas as a source of target tissue, as well as postponement of selection by 2 weeks and a lower selection pressure are important for successful transformation of oilseed rape.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of hypocotyl explants and a lower selection pressure is beneficial for transformation of economically important cultivars.

the use of a low concentration of kanamycin in combination with postponement of selection for a few days after co-culturing is a good strategy for the recovery of genetically modified plants from oilseed rape.
the transformation of oilseed rape can be improved by using cotyledonary petiolar explants from the seedlings obtained under dark conditions.
